title: Phonological Short Term Memory tasks for Italian-English comparison
author: Chiara Valeria Marinelli

steps_raw.instruction: Phonological Short Term Memory tasks
An attempt was made to develop tasks that would be comparable between the Italian (i.e., a consistent orthography) and English (i.e., an inconsistent orthography)versions.
Phonological STM was measured by a non-word repetition and a digit span tasks.
Non-word repetition task

Ten lists of three bi-syllabic (5 letters) non-words were read aloud with a pace of about one every 2 second. The child was asked to repeat each list as accurately as possible as soon as the experimenter finished speaking it. Each correct non-word was awarded a point out of a maximum score of 30.
“I am going to say some invented words. Please listen carefully and repeat them immediately after me, in the same order.”

The child was asked to repeat a list of digits read by the experimenter with an interval of about two second between them maintaining the same order of presentation. The task started with lists of four digits and progressed with longer lists. Ten lists were presented for each length. The task ended when the subject could not recall more than two lists of a given length. If the child made any mistake with the four digits lists, lists of three digits were presented as well. Otherwise, scoring assumes that performance with lists of two and three digits is completely correct. In the scoring each sequence recalled correctly is assigned 0.1 point. Thus, each length --which has ten lists--, contributes one point to the span if recalled completely correctly.
For the children: “I am going to say some numbers. Please listen carefully and repeat them immediately after me, in the same order.”

For the examiner: “Start with L=4. Read the numbers with about 1 sec. interval between them. If any mistakes are produced with L=4, do L=3. End the task when the subject cannot recall more than 2 sequences for a certain length.”
Digit span=..........

Each sequence recalled correctly=0.1 point (10 correct sequences =1 point). The span is the sum of the scores obtained for each length. If all sequences are recalled correctly for L=4, start the score from 4.
L=4 > 10/10 correct > score = 4.0 +
